content: 1. Nafcillin may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 6. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of riociguat by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentration. 20. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 21. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of warfarin through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. The less potent R-enantiomer of warfarin is partially metabolized by CYP3A4 (and also CYP1A2 and CYP2C19). Monitor INR more frequently if co-administered with inducers of these isoenzymes and adjust warfarin dose as needed. 50. Nafcillin and willow bark may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 51.
